v1-blocked-is-not-complete.title: Does a crew that BLOCKS get recorded as completed?
v1-blocked-is-not-complete.imperative: THE DECISIVE ITEM. Completion for a spine-only dispatch is now spine_terminal(), which returns True when checklist_engine.active_id(...) is None. A crew that hits a check it cannot satisfy is supposed to block and ask up (human ruling: 'always ask up'). Determine exactly what active_id returns for a spine whose gate is BLOCKED, HALTED, or skipped-with-refusals. If a blocked spine reads terminal, then a crew that correctly gave up is recorded as a clean success and the dispatching Commander is told the work is done. That is worse than the bug this rework fixed, and it is a BLOCK. Drive real spines into each of those states and report what happened.
v1-blocked-is-not-complete.finding: THE NAMED FEAR IS UNFOUNDED; TWO OTHER FALSE POSITIVES ARE REAL. checklist_engine.TERMINAL = {"complete","skipped"} — `blocked` is NOT in it. I drove real spines through the engine CLI (justified below) and read spine_terminal on each: [A] all gates complete -> True. [B] g1 blocked mid-spine, g2 pending -> False. [C] g1 complete, LAST gate blocked -> False. So a crew that correctly blocks and asks up is recorded `failed`, not `completed`. The decisive question answers correctly and does not block. What DOES read terminal: [D] every gate `skipped` -> True. [E] g1 complete, g2's postcondition REFUSED then `skip`ped with a reason -> True. `skip` is in the crew tool grant (spine_halt), needs only a reason and no authority, so a crew that hits a check it cannot satisfy has a self-serve exit that records as clean success — against the human ruling "always ask up". Journaled with a mandatory reason and visible in the spine, so: observation + triage candidate, not the blocker. [F] BLOCKING, reproduced with a REAL DISPATCH: a `survey`-typed spine whose every item is recorded but which was never consolidated reads terminal True. Live run — `run_crew.py --role reviewer --spine SURVEY.json` with no --handoff/--result — registry: `status: completed, result: null`; survey: both items `complete`, `consolidation: None`. A reviewer crew that produced NO VERDICT is reported to the dispatching Commander as done, with the verdict nowhere. active_id only walks item statuses and never looks at `consolidation`; it is a gated-spine API used to answer a survey question. Reachability is high: --spine accepts any checklist type, the spine-only prompt is type-agnostic ("Drive it gate by gate ... until it reports done"), reviewer/interrogator checklists ARE surveys (this very survey is one), and reviewer/SKILL.md names stopping-before-consolidate as "the single most common failure at this tier". [G] Also terminal: `{}` and `{"items": []}` — directly contradicting spine_terminal's own docstring, "A missing/unparseable/malformed spine is never terminal". Genuinely-missing and unparseable files DO return False; it is the valid-JSON-wrong-shape case that leaks. CLI DISCLOSURE: probes ran through `scripts/checklist_engine.py` because my door is bound to my own survey via SPINE_FILE and cannot bind a scratch spine — a tooling limit, not a preference. Every claim about the branch's own behaviour came from run_crew and real dispatches.

v2-real-spine-only-run.title: Run a real spine-only crew and confirm it is now recorded completed
v2-real-spine-only-run.imperative: The previous reviewer's probe found the failed-status bug by dispatching a real crew. Do it again against the fixed code: scratch spine, real dispatch with --spine and NO --handoff and no --result, and confirm the registry records completed. Then run the negative: a crew that leaves a gate open must still record failed. Both directions.
v2-real-spine-only-run.finding: Both directions proven by real dispatches against the fixed code, no fakes. POSITIVE: scratch 1-gate spine, `python scripts/run_crew.py --work-id probe2-rev2 --gate p1 --role implementer --model sonnet --spine .../probe2/POS.json --backend cli` with NO --handoff and NO --result -> printed `crew constellation/probe2-rev2/p1/implementer/attempt-1 -> completed`. Registry entry: handoff null, result null, spine bound, exit_code 0, result_present false, result_fresh false, status completed. The crew really drove the spine: g1 complete with c1 satisfied, and it wrote the file the imperative asked for (pos.txt = PROBE-POS-OK). This is the round-1 bug, now fixed and reproduced live — the same shape that was recorded `failed` before. NEGATIVE: 2-gate spine whose g2 imperative told the crew to leave the gate pending -> `crew .../p2neg/implementer/attempt-1 -> failed`, exit_code 0, spine statuses {g1: complete, g2: pending}. So the launcher recorded `failed` on a child that exited 0, purely on the spine read. The check is not a check that cannot fail.

v3-engine-import.title: run_crew.py now imports checklist_engine at module scope
v3-engine-import.imperative: New coupling between the launcher and the engine. The last module-scope import question in this wave was load-bearing -- importing mcp_spine_server requires a bound spine because it reads SPINE_FILE at import. Check what checklist_engine does at import time, whether run_crew can still be imported and run in every context that used to work (installed skills, a bare checkout, no spine bound), and whether any import cycle exists.
v3-engine-import.finding: BLOCKING REGRESSION — but not the import the item names. `checklist_engine` is clean at import: stdlib-only top-level imports, no os.environ/SPINE_FILE read at module scope (grep finds none), no reference to run_crew so no cycle, and it IS an explicitly listed companion of both bundles that ship run_crew.py. The load-bearing one is its neighbour. The SAME commit (2152ded3) also added `import install_constellation` at module scope — and install_constellation.py is NOT in any bundle that carries run_crew.py. Proven by running the real installer, not by reading it: `python scripts/install_constellation.py --agent claude --scope project --dest /tmp/instsim/skills --skills commander --force` produces a scripts/ dir with checklist_engine.py and no install_constellation.py; invoking that installed launcher from an unrelated directory gives `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'install_constellation'` at run_crew.py line 43, exit 1, before argparse. Same for the explorer bundle. TWO-SIDED: I installed main@9d593e0a the same way and ran the identical command — usage text, exit 0. So run_crew.py works from an installed skill on main and is dead on this branch. This is not a corner: global-everyone.md tells every role to "reference bundled scripts by their absolute installed path", and the Commander skill's standing instruction is to run every crew dispatch through run_crew.py. Commander and Explorer cannot launch any crew from an installed install. It survives the suite because the companion guard is hardcoded — tests/test_install_constellation.py reads `SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS.get("checklist_engine.py", ())`, so it can only ever check that one script's siblings. The fix is one entry: `"run_crew.py": ("install_constellation.py",)` in SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS (plus whatever install_constellation itself pulls in), and a guard keyed on every declared script rather than one literal.

v4-hook-still-fails-open.title: The hook is portable now; is it still silent when it breaks?
v4-hook-still-fails-open.imperative: sys.executable and shell:bash fix the two known failure paths. The underlying property remains: a PreToolUse hook that errors lets the call through. Say what residual failure modes still fail open, whether any of them are reachable, and whether the change acknowledges that anywhere a future author would see it. An accepted risk stated is fine; an unstated one is not.
v4-hook-still-fails-open.finding: The two named modes are genuinely fixed. Four residual modes remain; one is reachable and defeats the mechanism outright, and NONE is acknowledged where a future author would see it. (1) REACHABLE, and the big one — SCOPE, not fail-open: the hook matcher is `mcp__spine__spine_evidence`, but `Bash` is in CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS and checklist_engine.py has a `waive` verb. I drove it: a crew shelling out to `checklist_engine.py waive g1 --cond c1 --authority crew --reason ... --force` waived its own unsatisfiable check, then advanced the gate to `complete`, and spine_terminal reads True. The hook guards the door while the crew holds the key to the side entrance. The human ruling this hook implements — "agent cannot waive itself, always ask up" — is not enforced, and the handoff itself records that the previous crew used the CLI for everything. Arguably pre-existing (Bash was granted in 832aeee7), but 2152ded3's commit subject claims the hook "cannot fail open", which is a stronger claim than the code supports. (2) REACHABLE: malformed or empty stdin to the hook program -> `json.load` raises, rc=1; an erroring PreToolUse hook is treated as no opinion, so the call proceeds. I ran the hook program directly: waive->deny JSON rc=0, attest->`{}` rc=0, malformed stdin->rc=1 JSONDecodeError, empty stdin->rc=1. (3) `"shell": "bash"` requires bash on PATH; on a Windows host without Git Bash the hook cannot run at all -> fail open. The docstring justifies adding shell:bash by the non-POSIX parse hazard but never notes that it trades that for a hard bash dependency. (4) An interpreter moved/removed between dispatch and hook fire -> cannot run -> fail open. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: run_crew.py says "fail open" only about the two modes it FIXED (lines 431-432, 440). Nothing states the standing property — a PreToolUse hook that errors permits the call, so this denial is best-effort — and nothing mentions the Bash/CLI bypass. The item says an accepted risk stated is fine; it is not stated, so this records fail. A comment block naming (1) and (2) as accepted, plus dropping the overclaim in the commit-message-derived docstring, would satisfy it without new machinery.

v5-no-regression.title: Existing dispatches must be untouched
v5-no-regression.imperative: The handoff-branch prompt was byte-identical before; the argv is not (shell key, settings, two more granted tools, optional --result). Prove no existing dispatch path changed behaviour. Include: --result still required when no --spine is given, and both-given still judged the old way.
v5-no-regression.finding: The COMPLETION-JUDGMENT contract is clean; the ARGV path is not. Judgment matrix, driven directly through finalize_from_exit_code (exit 0 / exit 1 each): result-only + fresh -> completed/failed; result-only + missing -> failed/failed; BOTH given, spine terminal but result missing -> failed (result still rules); BOTH given, spine blocked but result fresh -> completed (result still rules); spine-only terminal -> completed/failed; spine-only blocked -> failed. Exactly the claim: --result given is judged as before, both-given keeps the old result-based rule, nonzero exit always fails. CLI refusals also hold: --handoff with no --result and no --spine is REFUSED. Handoff-branch prompt is byte-identical to main (asserted by comparing build_crew_argv output against main@9d593e0a's module). WHAT DID MOVE, for EVERY dispatch and not just spine-only ones: build_crew_argv now calls crew_settings_json() unconditionally, and crew_settings_json calls assert_shell_safe_command on `shlex.quote(sys.executable) + " -c '...'"`. When sys.executable contains a space, shlex.quote wraps it in single quotes, the guard refuses any command not starting with a bare word, and crew_settings_json RAISES. I reproduced it: '/opt/Program Files/py/python.exe' and 'C:\\Program Files\\Python312\\python.exe' both -> InstallError. Python under Program Files is a stock Windows install. On such a host NO crew can be dispatched at all — classic --handoff --result dispatches included. It is fail-closed and loud, not silent, which is why it is a regression rather than a safety hole; but it is a total-loss regression on a platform this repo documents at length, it contradicts the docstring's own claim that shlex.quote "covers an interpreter path containing spaces", and HookPortabilityTests only ever exercises the running host's own space-free sys.executable, so nothing catches it. Combined with v3, two of the three argv/settings changes made this dispatch path strictly worse than main on hosts other than this one.

(4) An interpreter moved/removed between dispatch and hook fire -> cannot run -> fail open. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: run_crew.py says "fail open" only about the two modes it FIXED (lines 431-432, 440). Nothing states the standing property — a PreToolUse hook that errors permits the call, so this denial is best-effort — and nothing mentions the Bash/CLI bypass. The item says an accepted risk stated is fine; it is not stated, so this records fail. A comment block naming (1) and (2) as accepted, plus dropping the overclaim in the commit-message-derived docstring, would satisfy it without new machinery.

v5-no-regression: The COMPLETION-JUDGMENT contract is clean; the ARGV path is not. Judgment matrix, driven directly through finalize_from_exit_code (exit 0 / exit 1 each): result-only + fresh -> completed/failed; result-only + missing -> failed/failed; BOTH given, spine terminal but result missing -> failed (result still rules); BOTH given, spine blocked but result fresh -> completed (result still rules); spine-only terminal -> completed/failed; spine-only blocked -> failed. Exactly the claim: --result given is judged as before, both-given keeps the old result-based rule, nonzero exit always fails. CLI refusals also hold: --handoff with no --result and no --spine is REFUSED. Handoff-branch prompt is byte-identical to main (asserted by comparing build_crew_argv output against main@9d593e0a's module). WHAT DID MOVE, for EVERY dispatch and not just spine-only ones: build_crew_argv now calls crew_settings_json() unconditionally, and crew_settings_json calls assert_shell_safe_command on `shlex.quote(sys.executable) + " -c '...'"`. When sys.executable contains a space, shlex.quote wraps it in single quotes, the guard refuses any command not starting with a bare word, and crew_settings_json RAISES. I reproduced it: '/opt/Program Files/py/python.exe' and 'C:\\Program Files\\Python312\\python.exe' both -> InstallError. Python under Program Files is a stock Windows install. On such a host NO crew can be dispatched at all — classic --handoff --result dispatches included. It is fail-closed and loud, not silent, which is why it is a regression rather than a safety hole; but it is a total-loss regression on a platform this repo documents at length, it contradicts the docstring's own claim that shlex.quote "covers an interpreter path containing spaces", and HookPortabilityTests only ever exercises the running host's own space-free sys.executable, so nothing catches it. Combined with v3, two of the three argv/settings changes made this dispatch path strictly worse than main on hosts other than this one.
consolidation.summary: BLOCK on two reproduced defects, one of them a total-loss regression. The question the handoff said would decide the verdict answers SAFELY: `blocked` is not in checklist_engine.TERMINAL, so a crew that correctly blocks and asks up is recorded `failed`, never `completed` (driven on real spines, mid-spine and last-gate). The spine-only contract itself works — a real dispatch with no --handoff and no --result recorded `completed`, and the negative control (open gate, exit 0) recorded `failed`. BLOCKER 1 (v3): commit 2152ded3 added `import install_constellation` at module scope to run_crew.py, but install_constellation.py ships in no bundle that carries run_crew.py. The installed commander and explorer launchers die with ModuleNotFoundError at import, before argparse; main@9d593e0a's installed launcher runs fine from the identical invocation. Every Commander and Explorer running from an installed install can launch no crew at all. The repo documents this exact drift class at install_constellation.py:80-88 and the guard that should catch it is hardcoded to checklist_engine.py. One SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS entry fixes it. BLOCKER 2 (v1): spine_terminal answers a `survey` question with `active_id`, a gated-spine API that never reads `consolidation`. A real reviewer crew dispatched spine-only that recorded every item and produced no verdict was recorded `completed`. That is the false-positive class the handoff named as worse than the round-1 bug, in the role whose entire deliverable is the verdict, and it is the failure reviewer/SKILL.md calls the most common at this tier. ALSO FAILING, non-blocking on their own: v5 — a `sys.executable` containing a space makes crew_settings_json raise, so no dispatch of any kind works on a stock Windows Python-under-Program-Files install, contradicting the docstring's claim that shlex.quote covers it; v4 — the waive-deny hook is bypassable by a crew shelling out to the engine CLI with `waive --force` (reproduced), and no residual fail-open mode is acknowledged anywhere a future author would see; r3/r4 — no test reaches blocked, skipped, unconsolidated-survey, malformed-spine, installed-bundle import, or a spaced interpreter. Two triage candidates flagged (crew self-serve `skip`; the Bash waive bypass). Scope is clean: all five hard no-gos respected, map/INDEX.md reproduces byte-exact, nothing pushed to main.

triage_candidates.statement: A crew can `skip` a gate whose check it cannot satisfy and be recorded `completed`. `spine_halt action=skip` is in CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS and needs only a reason, no authority; `skipped` is in checklist_engine.TERMINAL, so an all-skipped or partly-skipped spine reads terminal (reproduced: gate whose postcondition REFUSED, then skipped -> spine_terminal True). This is a self-serve exit from the human ruling "a crew that hits a check it cannot satisfy must block and ask up". Out of scope for this change (it is the crew tool grant and the engine's TERMINAL set, both no-go files here), but it is the same shape as the waive-deny hook and deserves the same treatment: deny `skip` to a crew, or require an authority the crew does not have.

The waive-deny hook is bypassable via Bash. `Bash` is in CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS and the PreToolUse matcher covers only `mcp__spine__spine_evidence`, so a crew can run `python scripts/checklist_engine.py waive <gate> --cond <c> --authority crew --reason ... --force` and waive its own bound check; I reproduced it end to end (waive accepted, gate advanced to complete, spine_terminal True). The human ruling the hook implements is therefore unenforced against any crew that reaches for the CLI — which the handoff records the previous crew doing. Out of scope for this change (fixing it means touching the tool grant, the engine, or adding a Bash-matcher hook). Candidate fixes: a second PreToolUse hook matching Bash that denies engine `waive` invocations, or teaching checklist_engine to refuse `waive` when the caller's session is a crew-keyed SPINE_SESSION.
